name: NeuroSurge
model_scope: Separate model under development; no trained decoder is supplied or validated by this game.
signal_origin: simulated, unitless brain and muscle activity values
source_lineage: Body update (R558), built from the 10 November interaction update: a camera at your eyes with a 90-degree view; a long-sitting body with every limb straight forward; the mirror body as a literal reflection on the same ground; 54 motor areas, one colour each, shared by the brain area and its muscles on both bodies, with a power-up glow; movements held until the opposite area or Reset body; F to hold and carry the brain, the mirror body or a limb; the Space dance; stop-at-contact between the three items; a closed skull, eyes and 111 more muscles from BodyParts3D and Z-Anatomy; a Borderlands-style cel-shaded comic look with black ink outlines, inked folds on the motor strip and an HDR glow; symmetric placement of paired controls; several performance passes. DESIGN-DECISIONS.md sections 20-53 record each change and why. The input-robustness changes published on 11 November (input epochs, deferred input, pointer capture and their four test files) are not in this version; they are being ported.
anatomy_assets: 611 human-anatomy OBJ files. BodyParts3D 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), including the new packets bodyparts3d-head-r1 (cranium and eyes) and missing-muscles-r1 (93 files); Z-Anatomy derivatives (CC BY-SA 4.0): the face muscles and 18 back, belly, neck and foot muscles in missing-muscles-r1. Packet files are unchanged archive members or documented conversions; runtime transforms, lifting, smoothing of finger and toe tips, colouring, comic shading and separated layers are display changes, not physiological validation.
code_licence: Project-owned contributions: CC0-1.0. Third-party material retains its own licences and notices.
known_engineering_gaps: The 11 November input-robustness work (pointer capture boundaries, stale-input cancellation, deferred input queue) is not in this version; its earlier failures and fixes do not carry over.
Frame rate: idle 60 fps, but the Space dance, look sweeps and carries draw about 26-33 fps in the author's single-core tests; a performance pass is under way.
A one-way look lock can occur after a far side look while an item rests against you; a fix is under way.
Some muscles still show pointed edges (for example at the base of the neck and the shoulder); a geometry check and fix are under way.
The crosshair caption naming the part under the crosshair is shown at all times; it is to move to the side panel with an on/off switch.
Joint mechanics, whole-body coupling, motor-area registration and timing remain simplified and unvalidated.
launcher_scope: Online URL launchers for Windows, macOS and Linux. Formats checked; native Windows/macOS use unverified. Prior Linux installation/launch does not prove execution of this updated target.
publication_status: Experimental preview published at the user's direct instruction of 12 November 2026, before the project's independent review. Check the displayed online version before assuming it matches these files.

browser_verification.scope: Author development checks only: scripted mouse and key input in one desktop Chromium on one pinned processor core, with screenshots and frame-interval counts, plus code reading and node checks by other instances of the same model that wrote it. No independent review yet. Not checked: Firefox, Safari, touch, phones, screen readers, reduced-motion settings in a browser.
